alternatives.option: Built-in automatic failover to a configured secondary after repeated failures.
alternatives.whyRejected: No single policy works predictably across the possible topologies, and an uncoordinated client-side failover is dangerous.

alternatives.option: No run-time reconfiguration at all; require a restart to change endpoints.
alternatives.whyRejected: Would prevent applications from implementing their own coordinated failover signal.

fields.consequences: ArgentSea stays out of the failover decision. The circuit breaker prevents pile-ups while a database is down, but recovery depends on infrastructure or application code. Applications that want client-driven failover must build the trigger and coordination themselves, using updatable connection properties.
fields.context: High-availability and disaster-recovery designs vary widely. A real failover usually involves coordinated infrastructure changes and a business decision. A single client that independently decides to fail over can split traffic across primaries and corrupt data.
fields.decision: ArgentSea does not fail a connection over to a standby server on its own. Failover is delegated to the infrastructure (DNS, availability-group listeners, the provider's FailoverPartner or multi-subnet settings) or to application code. Application code can redirect connections at run time by updating endpoint properties in the configuration hierarchy, and those changes propagate to inheriting connections.
fields.title: Leave database failover to infrastructure; make it possible, not automatic

sources.label: Failover boundary and configuration update capability
